```{r, message=FALSE}
# read in sce 
sce <- readr::read_rds(params$sce_file)

# validation groups and marker gene table urls 
validation_groups_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$validation_groups_file) |> 
  # rename final assigned group to avoid conflicts when merging in marker gene expression 
  # we want to separate the marker gene group from the actual cell type annotation
  dplyr::select(consensus_annotation, broad_celltype_group = validation_group_annotation)

# read in validation markers
markers_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$marker_genes_file) |> 
  # only keep genes unique to a single cell type except HPC which doesn't have any unique genes
  # for HPC we keep all 6 marker genes
  dplyr::filter(gene_observed_count == 1 | validation_group_annotation == "hematopoietic precursor cell")

# define color palette
celltype_colors <- readr::read_tsv(params$color_palette_file) |> 
  tibble::deframe()
# add greys for unknown and other 
celltype_colors[["unknown"]] <- "gray60"
celltype_colors[["other"]] <- "black"

# read in aucell results 
aucell_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$aucell_results_file)
ref_aucell_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$ref_aucell_file)

# read in reference annotations and gene set info 
ref_celltypes_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$ref_annotations_file) |>
  # only using the annotations from this file
  dplyr::select(barcodes, unique_id, consensus_celltype_annotation)
geneset_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$gene_set_category_file)

# read in infercnv results 
infercnv_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$infercnv_results_file)
```

```{r}
# get coldata for umap 
coldata_df <- scuttle::makePerCellDF(
    sce,
    use.coldata = c("barcodes", "consensus_celltype_annotation"),
    use.dimred = "UMAP"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
      "UMAP1" = "UMAP.1",
      "UMAP2" = "UMAP.2"
    ) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(validation_groups_df, by = c("consensus_celltype_annotation" = "consensus_annotation")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    unique_id = params$unique_id,
    broad_celltype_group = dplyr::if_else(
      is.na(broad_celltype_group),
      "unknown",
      broad_celltype_group
    )
  )
```

# Normal cell types

This section shows the normal cell types in this sample based on their consensus cell type annotations output by `scpca-nf`.
Consensus cell types are defined by first annotating cells using two different methods, [`SingleR`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SingleR.html) ([Looney _et al._ 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-018-0276-y)) with the `BlueprintEncodeData` reference from [`celldex`](http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/html/celldex.html) and [`CellAssign`](https://github.com/Irrationone/cellassign) ([Zhang _et al._ 2019](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-019-0529-1)) using marker genes for bone and soft tissue from [`PanglaoDB`](https://panglaodb.se/). 
Cells that map to related cell type ontology terms using both methods are assigned a consensus cell type. 
Any cells with disagreement between the two annotation methods are labeled as `unknown` and may be more likely to be tumor cells. 
More information on how cell types are assigned can be found in the [ScPCA Portal documentation](https://scpca.readthedocs.io/en/stable/processing_information.html#cell-type-annotation). 

Cell types are then grouped into broader cell type groups, e.g., all T cell types will be grouped together as T cells for the plots shown in this report. 

## Table of cell types 

```{r}
coldata_df |> 
  dplyr::count(consensus_celltype_annotation, broad_celltype_group, name = "Total") |> 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Total)) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
    "Consensus cell type" = consensus_celltype_annotation,
    "Broad cell type group" = broad_celltype_group
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```


## UMAPs

The below UMAPs shows the top 8 broad cell type groups. 
The first UMAP shows all cells together and the second UMAP is faceted by cell type, where the cells belonging to the specified cell type are in color and all other are in light grey. 
Any cells labeled with "other" include all normal cells that are not part of the top 8 cell type groups. 

```{r}
coldata_df <- coldata_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    broad_group_lumped = forcats::fct_lump_n(broad_celltype_group, 8, other_level = "other", ties.method = "first") |>
      forcats::fct_infreq() |>
      forcats::fct_relevel("unknown", "other", after = Inf)
  )

ggplot(coldata_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = broad_group_lumped)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = celltype_colors) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(color = "Broad cell type group")
```

```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=7}
faceted_umap(
  coldata_df,
  annotation_column = broad_group_lumped,
  celltype_colors = celltype_colors,
  point_size = 0.2
)
```


## Expression of marker genes 

This section looks at expression of a set of marker genes for each normal cell type across all cells. 
The dot plot shows the mean expression and percent of cells expressing the marker gene for cells from each broad cell type group. 
The y-axis includes marker genes for each cell type. 
Marker genes are obtained from the list of Human cell markers on [`CellMarker2.0`](http://www.bio-bigdata.center/CellMarker_download.html). 
All marker genes shown were specific to a single cell type, with the exception of hematopoietic precursor cells, if present, which express genes found in other, more differentiated immune cells. 

We expect that each cell type group should show high expression of marker genes associated with that cell type compared to all other cells in the dataset. 

Note that dots are only shown if the gene has mean expression > 0 and is expressed in at least 10% of the cells in the given cell type. 

```{r}
# extract gene expression for marker genes from SCE 
# list of all marker genes
all_markers <- markers_df |>
  dplyr::pull(ensembl_gene_id) |>
  unique()

# we only care about if that gene is expressed otherwise we won't waste memory and include it
expressed_genes <- rowData(sce) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(detected > 0) |>
  dplyr::pull(gene_ids)

# get markers that are expressed
expressed_markers <- intersect(all_markers, expressed_genes)

# get logcounts from sce for expressed genes
gene_exp_df <- scuttle::makePerCellDF(
  sce,
  features = expressed_markers,
  assay.type = "logcounts",
  use.coldata = "barcodes",
  use.dimred = FALSE
) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with("ENSG"), names_to = "ensembl_gene_id", values_to = "logcounts") |>
  dplyr::mutate(detected = logcounts > 0,
                unique_id = params$unique_id) 

# Join all consensus results and marker gene info
all_info_df <- coldata_df |>
  dplyr::left_join(gene_exp_df, by = c("barcodes", "unique_id")) |>
  # add marker gene information (associated validation group annotation, gene observed count, percent tissues)
  # account for the same gene being present in multiple cell types
  dplyr::left_join(markers_df, by = "ensembl_gene_id", relationship = "many-to-many")
```


```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=15}
marker_gene_dotplot(
  consensus_df = all_info_df,
  validation_groups_df = validation_groups_df,
  markers_df = markers_df,
  celltype_colors = celltype_colors,
  min_cells = 0 #TODO: Update this if needed to remove some cell types
)
```

# `AUCell` summary 

The plots in this section will look at the results from running [`AUCell`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/AUCell.html) across a set of gene sets obtained from `MSigDB` and custom gene lists. 
Information about the gene sets used here can be found in [`ews-nf/genesets`](https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/ews-nf/tree/main/genesets). 

Plots here show the z-score calculated from the AUC reported by `AUCell`. 
For each gene set, the mean and standard deviation of the AUC values for all reference cells was used to contain a z-score for all cells. 
Cell types are colored based on whether or not the cell type is part of the reference or query cell types, where query is broken up into "unknown" and normal non-malignant cell types (labeled as "normal non-reference") based on consensus cell type labels. 
If any unknown or normal non-malignant cell types show gene expression patterns expected to be observed in tumor cells, it's likely that those cells are mis-classified and are in fact tumor cells. 

Gene sets can be divided into three groups to help distinguish tumor cells from normal cells:  

* `EF-activated`: These gene sets contain genes that are activated by the fusion gene, `EWS::FLI1`. 
We expect any cells with high z-scores relative to reference cells to be tumor cells. 
* `EF-repressed`: These gene sets contain genes that are repressed by the fusion gene, `EWS::FLI1`. 
We expect any cells with low z-scores relative to reference cells to be tumor cells.
* `EMT-ECM`: These gene sets contain genes that are found to be highly expressed in tumor cells with low expression of `EWS::FLI1`.

We expect tumor cells to have high expression of genes that are activated by `EWS::FLI1` and low expression of genes that are repressed by `EWS::FLI1`, indicating high activity of the `EWS::FLI1` fusion. 
It's likely there could also be a population of tumor cells that are `EWS::FLI1` "low". 
We expect those cells to have lower expression of the activated genes and higher expression of the repressed genes along with an EMT-like phenotype. 


```{r, message=FALSE}
# assign broad cell type categories to all reference cells
ref_celltypes_df <- ref_celltypes_df |> 
  dplyr::select(barcodes, unique_id, consensus_celltype_annotation) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(validation_groups_df, by = c("consensus_celltype_annotation" = "consensus_annotation")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    broad_celltype_group = dplyr::if_else(
      is.na(broad_celltype_group),
      "unknown",
      broad_celltype_group
    )
  )

# combine infor for all cells for the given library with the reference cells 
celltype_df <- coldata_df |>
  dplyr::full_join(ref_celltypes_df)

# combine all aucell results
all_aucell_df <- aucell_df |> 
  # add zscores for reference cells
  dplyr::full_join(ref_aucell_df) |> 
  # add gene set categories
  dplyr::left_join(geneset_df, by = c("gene_set" = "geneset_name")) |> 
  # include consensus and broad cell types 
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_df, by = c("barcodes", "unique_id")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # add cell category and set levels for cell and gene set categories
    cell_category = dplyr::case_when(
      ref_or_query == "reference" ~ "reference",
      broad_celltype_group == "unknown" ~ "unknown",
      .default = "normal non-reference"
    ) |> 
      forcats::fct_relevel("unknown", after = 0),
    geneset_category = factor(geneset_category, levels = c("EF-activated", "EF-repressed", "EMT-ECM"))
  )

# define color palettes for AUCell and inferCNV plots 
cell_category_colors <- brewer.pal(n = 3, name = "Dark2")
names(cell_category_colors) <- unique(all_aucell_df$cell_category)
geneset_colors <- c("#00274C",  "#FFCB05", "gray80")
names(geneset_colors) <- unique(all_aucell_df$geneset_category)
```

## AUC Heatmap 

The heatmap below shows the mean z-score for each gene set across all cell types. 
As with the previous section, the broad cell type group is shown instead of the full consensus cell type. 

The annotation bar on the bottom indicates the gene set category (e.g., `EF-activated` and `EF-repressed`) and the annotation bar on the right indicates the cell type category (e.g., reference, unknown, or normal non-reference). 

```{r, message=FALSE}
# create mtx with mean zscore for heatmap 
auc_mtx <- all_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::group_by(broad_celltype_group, gene_set) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_zscore = mean(auc_zscore)
  ) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = gene_set, 
                     values_from = mean_zscore) |> 
  tidyr::drop_na() |> 
  tibble::column_to_rownames("broad_celltype_group") |>
  as.matrix()


# add ref or query annotation bars
ref_annotation_df <- all_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::distinct(broad_celltype_group, cell_category) |>
  tidyr::drop_na() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(broad_celltype_group = factor(broad_celltype_group, levels = rownames(auc_mtx))) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(broad_celltype_group)

ref_annotation <- ComplexHeatmap::rowAnnotation(
    cell_category = ref_annotation_df$cell_category,
    col = list(cell_category = cell_category_colors),
    annotation_label = c(cell_category = "Cell category"),
    show_annotation_name = FALSE
  )

# add gene set category annotation bars 
geneset_annotation_df <- all_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::distinct(gene_set, geneset_category) |>
  tidyr::drop_na() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(gene_set = factor(gene_set, levels = colnames(auc_mtx))) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(gene_set)

geneset_annotation <- ComplexHeatmap::columnAnnotation(
  geneset_category = geneset_annotation_df$geneset_category,
  col = list(geneset_category = geneset_colors),
  annotation_label = c(geneset_category = "Gene set \ncategory"),
  show_annotation_name = FALSE
)
```


```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
    auc_mtx,
    # set the color scale based on min and max values
    col = circlize::colorRamp2(seq(min(auc_mtx), max(auc_mtx), length = 2), colors = c("white", "#00274C")),
    border = TRUE,
    ## Row parameters
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    row_title = "Broad cell type group",
    row_title_side = "left",
    row_names_side = "left",
    row_dend_side = "right",
    row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10),
    ## Column parameters
    column_title = "Gene set",
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    column_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 8),
    bottom_annotation = geneset_annotation,
    right_annotation = ref_annotation,
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
      title = "Mean z-score"
    )
)
  
```

## Ridge plots 

The below ridge plot shows the distribution of z-scores for each gene set.
Cells are grouped based on if they are part of the reference or query, where query is broken up into "unknown" and normal non-malignant cell types based on consensus cell type labels. 

```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=8, message=FALSE}
# ridge plot faceted by geneset within each category
levels(all_aucell_df$geneset_category) |> 
  purrr::map(\(category){
    
    all_aucell_df |> 
      dplyr::filter(geneset_category == category) |> 
      ggplot(aes(x = auc_zscore, y = forcats::fct_rev(cell_category), fill = cell_category)) +
      ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5, scale = 1.5) +
      facet_wrap(vars(gene_set), ncol = 3) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
      labs(
        title = category,
        x = "z-score",
        y = "Cell type category"
      ) +
      theme(legend.position = "none")
    
  }) |>
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(6, 4, 2))
```


Below we calculated the mean z-score for all gene sets in a given gene set category (e.g., all gene sets that are part of `EF-activated`). 
We then look at the distribution of those mean z-scores across all cell types. 
Ridge plots for each cell type are colored based on whether or not the cell type is part of the reference or query cell types, where query is broken up into "unknown" and normal non-malignant cell types based on consensus cell type labels. 
Any cell type with less than 3 cells will not be included in the plot. 

```{r, message=FALSE}
# get the mean zscore for each gene set category 
grouped_aucell_df <- all_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::group_by(cell_id, broad_celltype_group, geneset_category, cell_category) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_category_zscore = mean(auc_zscore)
  ) 

# get total number of cells for each cell type
# need this to both label the axes and filter out any cell types that have too few cells
celltype_counts_df <- grouped_aucell_df |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::select(cell_id, broad_celltype_group) |> 
  dplyr::distinct() |> 
  dplyr::add_count(broad_celltype_group) |> 
  # add in y label 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = glue::glue("{broad_celltype_group} ({n})")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::select(broad_celltype_group, y_label, n) |> 
  dplyr::distinct()

# grab order of broad cell types based on cell type categories 
celltype_levels <- celltype_counts_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(ref_annotation_df) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(cell_category) |> 
  dplyr::pull(y_label) |>
  as.character()

# prep for ridge plot 
ridges_plot_df <- grouped_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_counts_df) |> 
  dplyr::filter(n >= 3) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = factor(y_label, levels = rev(celltype_levels))
  )
```


```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=15, message=FALSE}
ggplot(ridges_plot_df, aes(x = mean_category_zscore, y = y_label, fill = cell_category)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(geneset_category),
             ncol = 1,
             scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean z-score",
    y = "Broad cell type group",
    fill = "Cell type \ncategory"
  )
```


# InferCNV 

[`inferCNV`](https://github.com/broadinstitute/inferCNV/wiki) was run using all normal cell types that are listed in [`references/reference-celltype.tsv`](https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/ews-nf/blob/main/references/reference-celltypes.tsv) as a reference. 

## Heatmap 

Below is the heatmap showing chromosome gains and losses as output by `inferCNV`. 

![](`r params$infercnv_heatmap_file`)


## All CNVs

Below we look at the distribution of total CNVs detected per cell. 
The number of chromosomes with a detectable CNV is totaled and then the mean and standard deviation of the total CNV sum for all reference cells are used to calculate a z-score for all cells in the dataset. 

As with the `AUCell` results, cells are colored based on whether or not the cell type is part of the reference or query cell types, where query is broken up into "unknown" and normal non-malignant cell types (labeled as "normal non-reference") based on consensus cell type labels. 
We expect tumor cells to have higher numbers of CNVs than reference cells. 

The first plot shows all cell type groups (unknown, normal non-reference, and unknown) and then the second plot shows each broad cell type category. 
Only cell types with at least 3 cells are shown. 

### Ridge plots

```{r}
# read infercnv results
infercnv_df <- infercnv_df |>
  # indicator for reference vs query cell based on `subcluster` name
  dplyr::mutate(cell_group = stringr::str_split_i(subcluster, "_", 1)) |>
  # separate barcode and library
  tidyr::separate(
    cell_id,
    sep = "-",
    into = c("unique_id", "barcodes"),
    remove = FALSE
  ) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_df, by = c("barcodes", "unique_id")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # add cell category 
    cell_category = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(subcluster, "reference") ~ "reference",
      broad_celltype_group == "unknown" ~ "unknown",
      .default = "normal non-reference"
    ) |> 
      forcats::fct_relevel("unknown", after = 0) |>
      forcats::fct_rev()
  )

# calculate the total cnv sum for each cell 
sum_cnv_df <- infercnv_df |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    starts_with("has_cnv_"),
    names_to = "chr",
    values_to = "cnv"
  ) |>
  # sum all values for each
  dplyr::group_by(barcodes, unique_id) |>
  dplyr::summarize(total_cnv_per_cell = sum(cnv)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() 


# add back in to larger df with all cnv information and cell types 
all_cnv_df <- infercnv_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(sum_cnv_df, by = c("unique_id", "barcodes"))

# calculate a z-score for the total CNV using the reference cells as mean and sd
ref_cnv_sums <- all_cnv_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(cell_category == "reference") |> 
  dplyr::pull(total_cnv_per_cell)
ref_mean <- mean(ref_cnv_sums)
ref_sd <- sd(ref_cnv_sums)

# now add in zscore
all_cnv_df <- all_cnv_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    cnv_zscore = (total_cnv_per_cell - ref_mean)/ref_sd
  )
```


```{r, message = FALSE}
# ridge plot showing z-score of cnv sum 
ggplot(all_cnv_df, aes(x = cnv_zscore, y = cell_category, fill = cell_category)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
  labs(
    y = "",
    x = "CNV z-score"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r, message = FALSE}
# remove cell types with < 3 and set cell category levels
filtered_cnv_df <- all_cnv_df |> 
  # add in a y label and celltype counts
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_counts_df) |> 
  dplyr::filter(n >= 3) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = factor(y_label, levels = rev(celltype_levels))
  )


ggplot(filtered_cnv_df, aes(x = cnv_zscore, y = y_label, fill = forcats::fct_rev(cell_category))) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "z-score",
    y = "",
    fill = "Cell type \ncategory"
  )
```


## Ewing-specific CNVs

There are a few known copy number variations in Ewing's sarcoma: 

- Gain of Chr8
- Gain of Chr12
- Gain of Chr1p
- Loss of Chr16q

Although these are the most frequent, there are patients who do not have any of these alterations and patients that only have some of these alterations. 
See [Tirode _et al._ 2014](https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-14-0622) and [Crompton _et al._ 2014](https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-13-1037)

Below we look at the presence of these specific CNVs by showing the proportion of each chromosome that is part of any of the CNV events.
For each chromsome we show the proportions for gains, losses and total proportion. 

```{r, message=FALSE}
# define the chromosomes typically affected in Ews
validation_chr <- c("chr1", "chr8", "chr12", "chr16")

# get the proportion for each chromosome of interest split out by type (cnv, dupli, loss)
prop_cnv_df <- infercnv_df |>
  dplyr::select(
    starts_with("proportion_scaled_"),
    cell_id,
    unique_id,
    barcodes,
    subcluster
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    starts_with("proportion_scaled_"),
    names_to = "cnv_type_raw",
    values_to = "proportion"
  ) |>
  # more tidying
  dplyr::mutate(cnv_type_raw = stringr::str_remove(cnv_type_raw, "^proportion_scaled_")) |>
  tidyr::separate(cnv_type_raw, sep = "_", into = c("cnv_type", "chr")) |>
  # only care about validation chromosomes here 
  dplyr::filter(chr %in% validation_chr) |> 
  # set chr factors
  dplyr::mutate(
    chr = stringr::str_remove(chr, "^chr"),
    chr = factor(chr, levels = 1:22),
    cnv_type = dplyr::case_when(
      cnv_type == "cnv" ~ "total",
      cnv_type == "dupli" ~ "gain", 
      .default = cnv_type
    ),
    # create unique label to use for faceting 
    facet_label = glue::glue("chr{chr}-{cnv_type}")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(infercnv_df)
```

```{r, message = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=8}
ggplot(prop_cnv_df, aes(x = proportion, y = cell_category, fill = cell_category)) +
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(facet_label),
    scales = "free_x",
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion CNV",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# AUCell and CNV results 

Here we show UMAPs colored by the mean z-score for either the gene set category or sum CNV.
The UMAP is faceted by cell type category so that only cells from that category are included in the panel. 

```{r, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
# combine with umap_df and create faceted umap by mean auc for each geneset 
auc_umap_df <- grouped_aucell_df |> 
  dplyr::rename(
    method_category = geneset_category,
    zscore = mean_category_zscore
  )

cnv_umap_df <- all_cnv_df |> 
  dplyr::select(cell_id, broad_celltype_group, cell_category, zscore = cnv_zscore) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    method_category = "Total CNV"
  )

zscore_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(list(auc_umap_df, cnv_umap_df))

umap_df <- coldata_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    cell_id = glue::glue("{unique_id}-{barcodes}") 
  ) |> 
  dplyr::left_join(zscore_df, by = c("cell_id", "broad_celltype_group"))

ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = zscore)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(method_category),
             cols = vars(cell_category)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
  theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(0.02, "in"),
      aspect.ratio = 1
    ) +
  labs(color = "Mean z-score")

```

```{r}
combined_df <- all_cnv_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(grouped_aucell_df) |> 
  dplyr::select(barcodes, unique_id, UMAP1, UMAP2, geneset_category, cell_category, broad_celltype_group, broad_group_lumped, consensus_celltype_annotation, cnv_zscore, mean_category_zscore) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    geneset_category = glue::glue("auc-zscore_{geneset_category}")
  ) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = geneset_category,
    values_from = mean_category_zscore
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = `auc-zscore_EF-activated`, y = cnv_zscore, color = broad_group_lumped)) +

  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +

```

# Tumor cell assignment


Confident tumor cells - EF-activated > 2 + CNV > 2 
cnv tumor - CNV > 2 
low cells - CNV > 2 & EMT-ECM > 2 

```{r}
combined_df <- combined_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    combined_annotation = dplyr::case_when(
      cnv_zscore > 2 & `auc-zscore_EF-activated` > 2 ~ "tumor-combined",
      cnv_zscore > 2 & `auc-zscore_EMT-ECM` > 2 ~ "tumor-low",
      cnv_zscore > 2 ~ "tumor-cnv",
      `auc-zscore_EF-activated` > 2 & `auc-zscore_EF-repressed` < -1 ~ "tumor-aucell",
      .default = consensus_celltype_annotation
    ),
    tumor_annotation = dplyr::if_else(stringr::str_detect(tumor_annotation, "tumor"), "tumor", "non-malignant")
  )

table(combined_df$tumor_annotation, useNA = "ifany")
```


```{r}
tumor_annotation_colors <- unique(combined_df$combined_annotation)
colors <- palette.colors(n = length(tumor_annotation_colors), palette = "alphabet") |> 
  purrr::set_names(tumor_annotation_colors)

ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = combined_annotation)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors)
```


```{r, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
faceted_umap(
  combined_df,
  annotation_column = combined_annotation,
  celltype_colors = colors,
  point_size = 0.2
)
```

```{r}
total_counts_df <- combined_df |> 
  dplyr::count(combined_annotation) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = glue::glue("{combined_annotation} ({n})"),
    y_label = factor(y_label, levels = rev(unique(y_label)))
  )

filtered_annotations_df <- combined_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(total_counts_df) |> 
  dplyr::filter(n >=3 )
```


```{r, fig.height=15, fig.width=10}
geneset_columns <- colnames(filtered_annotations_df)[stringr::str_detect(colnames(filtered_annotations_df), "auc-zscore")]


c(geneset_columns, "cnv_zscore") |> 
  purrr::map(\(column){
    
    ggplot(filtered_annotations_df, aes(x = !!sym(column), y = y_label, fill = tumor_annotation)) +
      ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
      #scale_fill_manual(values = cell_category_colors) +
      labs(
        y = "",
        fill = ""
      )
    
  }) |> 
  patchwork::wrap_plots(guides = "collect", ncol = 1)
```
